absent: Numeric values, encodings and ordering of page levels, huge page ceilings and generation masks
Full object layouts for VM, slot, shadow page, fault and iterator beyond fields observed here
Contracts of TDP walk macros, root enumeration and reschedule helpers
Atomic entry install protocol and remote TLB flush scope and ordering
Legacy reverse map walk and handler return conventions
Guest mem and confidential computing backing negotiation and error sentinel recovery
MMIO caching policy, generation mask layout and wrap handling frequency
Address space count, identifier allocation and arch specific slot hooks on other architectures
Dirty bitmap allocation, lifetime and synchronization with clearing and logging
Execute control policy for huge pages and large page info population

findings.text: Provides a query that reports the largest page size usable for a guest frame within a slot. It honors a fault provided ceiling and privacy flag when a fault context exists, otherwise starts from the architectural maximum and derives privacy from memory attributes. The result is limited by a global huge page ceiling and by per size slot prohibitions, falling back to the smallest size when nothing larger is allowed, then further limited by host or guest mem backing capability.

Exposes a constructor that collapses a small present mapping into a large page entry for a requested level. It requires presence and a level above the smallest, marks the entry as large, aligns the address to the large page boundary while preserving non address bits, and optionally removes execute permission when large page execute control is active.

Serves as the slot wide dirty state clearing entry. For legacy reverse map tracking it clears only smallest granularity entries, while for TDP operation it delegates to a TDP slot clearer. It performs no TLB flush itself and relies on the caller to flush after return.

Huge page recovery over a slot range never operates while dirty tracking is active and skips entries that are absent, already leaves, above the allowable huge ceiling, outside the slot extent, or larger than the backing allows. Successful collapse installs one large entry atomically and requests a single batched TLB flush for the slot after the walk.

Host backing size is inferred by translating the guest frame through the slot userspace mapping and inspecting host table entries with single reads. Missing or non present entries stop the inspection at the smallest size, a large pud observation reports the 1G size, a large pmd observation reports the 2M size, otherwise the smallest size is reported.

Guest to host address translation derives an offset from slot base, clamps it against slot size with a speculation barrier so mispredicted loads cannot escape the registered range, then scales by page size and adds the slot userspace base.

Guest mem backing size uses fault resolved frame and ceiling when fault context exists. Without fault context it currently falls back to the smallest size and signals incomplete hugepage support. A confidential computing hook may further restrict the ceiling, where a zero return means no extra restriction.

Slot exclusivity and frame privacy are reported by small predicates. Exclusivity is false when guest mem support is compiled out, otherwise it reflects a slot flag. Privacy either reflects a memory attribute query for the private bit or is constantly false, depending on build configuration.

TDP huge construction looks inside the child table of a non leaf entry over the large page extent and uses the first present leaf found to build the collapsed entry. It reports a retry signal if rescheduling is needed during the scan and a not found signal when no present leaf exists.

Dirty tracking enablement is a slot flag test. CPU assisted dirty logging updates are skipped entirely when the VM has no CPU log buffer. Otherwise a broadcast request is issued when enabling the first tracked slot or when no tracked slots remain.

TDP dirty clearing walks each valid root for the slot address space over the slot extent and atomically clears a selected bit only on present leaves. The cleared bit is the writable bit when write protection is required for the tree, otherwise the dirty bit, with a warning if dirty bit mode encounters an entry that still needs protection.

Need for write protection is determined per tree from shadow page state and a global accessed dirty enable. A shadow page needs protection when CPU dirty logging is active and the page belongs to nested guest mode, because hardware logging would attribute L2 addresses. Entry level need is decided by comparing TDP accessed dirty bits against the enabled pattern, with a warning on absent entries.

Slot teardown leaves no remaining guest mem binding for flagged slots, no dirty bitmap, no arch specific slot state, and no slot allocation. Activation ensures the prepared set becomes active and the inactive set carries the same new descriptor for the resolved address space. Address space resolution yields the present side when one descriptor is missing, warns on disagreement, and yields zero when both are missing.

Replacement always edits the inactive set selected by the node index. Old identifier and host range nodes are removed and the cached last used pointer is forwarded. Deletion also removes the guest range node and stops. Otherwise the host interval is rebuilt from userspace base and page count, identifier and host range nodes are inserted, and the guest range node is either swapped in place when base is unchanged or removed and reinserted.

Guest range ordering is a binary tree keyed by slot base. Insertion walks left or right by base comparison and faults on duplicate base, then links and balances. Erasure removes the indexed node, while replacement swaps nodes in place after verifying equal bases.

Provides the post update hook invoked after a new slot generation is published. It refreshes MMIO shadow entry validity for the generation and kicks every virtual CPU to force reevaluation of cached state such as steal time.

MMIO shadow validity is tied to slot generations. The hook ignores calls while an update is flagged as in progress and does nothing when MMIO caching is disabled. Otherwise it masks the generation, strips the address space stride, and on wrap to zero discards all shadow pages with a rate limited notice.

Slot set publication moves through flagged, visible, and settled phases. The inactive set inherits the active generation plus an in progress mark, waits for ongoing invalidations, becomes visible via RCU assignment, releases the arch slots mutex, waits for SRCU readers, then clears the mark and advances by the address space count before invoking the arch hook and storing the final generation.

Fast full zap toggles a one bit MMU validity generation under exclusive locks so at most one obsolete generation coexists with valid pages, invalidates direct TDP roots when TDP is enabled, broadcasts a request for CPUs to drop obsolete roots, then reclaims obsolete pages. The front half runs under the write lock while the back half runs after release.

Huge recovery and dirty clearing share a retry discipline. A reschedule check may restart the current iterator position, an atomic install contention restarts the same entry, a collapsed entry sets a pending flush flag, and a single slot wide flush is emitted at the end only if at least one install succeeded.

Maximum mapping queries require the VM MMU lock held, TDP slot dirty clearing requires it held for read, and fast zap front half requires slots lock plus MMU write lock. Huge recovery and TDP dirty walks hold RCU read lock across iteration with explicit reschedule points. Host backing inspection disables interrupts across single read table loads to avoid races with concurrent table teardown or promotion.

Slot leaf dirty clearing takes the MMU write lock for the legacy reverse map walk and the read lock for the TDP walk, with TLB flushing deferred to the caller outside the locks. Generation publication serializes against invalidations with a dedicated spinlock and wait queue, publishes with RCU assignment, then drops the arch slots mutex before an expedited SRCU barrier to avoid deadlock with readers that acquire that mutex.

Each address space keeps two slot sets selected by a node index bit, with one active and one under construction. Slots are indexed three ways for the active index. Hashed by identifier, interval tree by host range derived from userspace base and page count, and ordered tree by guest base, plus a cached last used pointer that is forwarded on replacement.

Address translation observes slot base guest frame, page count, userspace base, flags, address space identifier and numeric identifier. Fault context when present carries a ceiling level, privacy flag and resolved frame. Slot large page info carries a per level prohibition flag consulted from large to small.

TDP iteration exposes current level, guest frame and prior entry value. Shadow page roles expose nesting mode used for write protect decisions, and VM arch state exposes CPU dirty log size and MMU validity generation. Entry state distinguishes presence, leaf status at a level, and accessed dirty enable pattern.

Querying large page info for a frame outside the slot would read out of bounds, so such iterators must be skipped. Unclamped guest controlled offsets could become speculation gadgets outside registered slots. Rereading host entries during promotion could mix old leaf status with new table address and misdirect the walk. Single reads plus interrupt masking mitigate teardown and promotion races.

Inserting a slot with duplicate guest base is fatal. Non fault guest mem size queries currently lack frame and order inputs and force smallest size with a one time warning. Collapsing a non present entry or requesting the smallest level violates an internal bug check, and clearing dirty state in dirty bit mode on an entry needing protection triggers a warning.

Publishing slot sets while invalidations run would unbalance invalidation locking, so publication waits. Releasing the arch slots mutex must precede the SRCU barrier to avoid deadlock. MMIO generations can wrap. The wrap case must discard all shadow pages, and in progress generations must never be treated as stable.

Facts observed include a page level hierarchy with 4K smallest, 2M intermediate, 1G large, a total count and a maximum huge page level. Also a page size bit marking large entries, address masks aligning to level and page boundaries, and writable, dirty and accessed dirty enable patterns selecting dirty tracking mode.

Facts observed include slot flags for dirty logging, guest mem binding and guest mem only, a private memory attribute bit, an error frame sentinel for faults, direct root and CPU and TLB request identifiers for broadcasts, and slot generation in progress and MMIO generation mask bits with generation striding by address space count.
